title: How Ruben Hassid grew LinkedIn to 770K followers with AI, taste and consistency
summary: Ruben argues AI made effort and strategy worthless, leaving taste and consistency as the real edge. He breaks LinkedIn growth into three levers: reader-centric (not personal) topics, pattern-breaking hooks, and scrappy useful media, then insists on daily posting and picking a target to pursue with action.

principles.text: Write posts about the reader's problem, not your achievements; nobody cares about you, they care about being helped.
principles.quote: Either I help YOU now, or you won’t care enough to follow me.

principles.text: AI makes effort and generic strategy worthless; what remains scarce is taste and consistency.
principles.quote: AI made what was valuable terribly easy: the effort to start & a reasonable strategy. Both are now worthless and won’t make you a Linkedin star.

principles.text: The hook is the first two lines; its only job is to break the scroll pattern and earn the 'more' click. Generate many variants and let taste pick.
principles.quote: You must shock the reader. Break his patterns. Wake him up from his slumber and doomscrolling.

principles.text: Media dominates the screen, so it matters more than body text; the best format is a scrappy, unbranded, useful single image, not an ad-looking asset.
principles.quote: the more it looks like an ad, the worse the post performs. Be scrappy.

principles.text: Post daily: volume produces learning, which sharpens taste. There is no prompt that replaces consistency.
Don't stand still waiting for the perfect goal; pick a target, pursue it with AI, and build an unfair advantage through action.
principles.quote: Make your advantage so unfair it feels insurmountable to catch up with you.
